report_name: AWS AgentCore Default Configs Risk Credential Exfiltration via Prompt Injection

attack_patterns.name: LLM Prompt Injection
attack_patterns.description: An attacker can craft input to trick the Large Language Model (LLM) powering the AWS AgentCore agent into executing a malicious command instead of its intended task, leading to credential exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
attack_patterns.description: The AI agent is manipulated via prompt injection to execute arbitrary bash commands through its built-in 'shell' tool, which runs with root privileges.

attack_patterns.name: Unsecured Credentials
attack_patterns.description: The agent's shell tool, executed via prompt injection, can access and exfiltrate plaintext credentials (like API keys) that are handled in the same memory space by AgentCore Identity.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: The AI agent itself acts as a public-facing application, and the prompt injection vector is used to exploit its default-enabled, high-privilege tools.

tools.name: AWS AgentCore Harness
tools.description: A managed runtime for AI agents whose default configuration is vulnerable to prompt injection leading to command execution.

tools.name: shell
tools.description: A built-in tool in AWS AgentCore Harness, enabled by default with root privileges, that can execute arbitrary bash commands. It is the primary mechanism for command execution following a prompt injection.

tools.name: file_operations
tools.description: A built-in tool in AWS AgentCore Harness, enabled by default, that can be used for file system manipulation.

tools.name: curl
tools.description: A network utility that can be executed by the agent's 'shell' tool to exfiltrate credentials or other data over the network.

tools.name: wget
tools.description: A network utility that can be executed by the agent's 'shell' tool to exfiltrate credentials or other data over the network.

tools.name: nc
tools.description: A network utility (netcat) that can be executed by the agent's 'shell' tool to exfiltrate credentials or other data over the network.

tools.name: printenv
tools.description: An environment inspection command that can be executed by the agent's 'shell' tool to discover plaintext credentials stored in environment variables.

vulnerabilities.name: AWS AgentCore Harness Insecure Default Configuration
vulnerabilities.description: A dangerous default configuration in AWS AgentCore Harness where the built-in 'shell' tool is enabled with root privileges, allowing prompt injection attacks to execute arbitrary commands and exfiltrate credentials.

identities.name: Amazon Web Services
identities.description: Vendor of the AWS AgentCore Harness product which has an insecure default configuration.

identities.name: Users of AWS AgentCore Harness
identities.description: Any user or organization building AI agents on the AWS AgentCore Harness platform without hardening the default configuration is potentially at risk of credential exfiltration.

indicators.name: Suspicious Command Execution from AI Agent
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Command Execution from AI Agent
id: 2f8b1c9a-7d3e-4f0a-8b1c-9a7d3e4f0a8b
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of suspicious network or environment inspection utilities which could indicate a compromised AI agent executing commands via an injected prompt.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/securing-aws-agentcore-harness-credentials/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-09-18
tags:
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.aml.t0051
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/curl'
      - '/wget'
      - '/nc'
      - '/printenv'
  filter_known_good:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/sshd'
      - '/bash'
      - '/zsh'
  condition: selection and not filter_known_good
indicators.description: Detects the execution of network or inspection utilities like curl, wget, nc, or printenv, which could indicate an AI agent being manipulated via prompt injection to exfiltrate data or inspect its environment for credentials.
